Australia's cricket summer is off to a spicy start

Amid this carnage came Mahli Beardman's debut, offering some refreshing actual action on the field. Imagine on your debut, transforming into the leader of the pace attack and taking a five-wicket haul in 28 balls. These are things that players and fans visualize executing in their alone time or when going to bed. But young Mahli manifested this to the T in Perth on Friday, bowling 140+, rushing batters with pace, bounce and lateral movement. The way England are playing (dancing to Mahli's tunes), looks like they have never played on a pitch with bounce, quipped Mark Waugh on air. Even captain Mitch Marsh was jokingly saying he wonders which member of the famed trio of Starc, Hazlewood, and Cummins will sit out for Mahli.

Harry Brook's team has had a rough time in their last 5 ODIs.

- Dramatic collapse from 91/0 to lose the run chase
- Losing after posting 429 on the board
- Conceding an 89-run last wicket stand to lose the game
- Being reduced to 65/8 while batting first

The story could worsen if England lose the toss in Adelaide as well.

The patterns in Adelaide

- Like Perth, since 2019, this venue heavily favours the chasing side.
- The last four ODI wins were achieved by the team batting second.
- In all those four games, the side batting first lost at least two wickets inside the first 10 overs.
- The only good news is that the average first innings score is much higher than Perth, standing at a decent 253.

So it is vital for Brook to call the toss right and bowl first to keep the series alive.

One thing is for sure. The ball won't bounce as much as it did in Perth, so the England batters need to pull up their socks and fight if they bat first for Jofra Archer and Co. to at least have a decent chance with the ball. Jofra got some lovely swing at pace in the first ODI and he should make the ball move here as well. Do watch out for his battle with Travis Head as he will look to trouble the left-hander with outswing. Interestingly, Travis averages 65.80 at this venue in ODIs with 2 fifties and 1 hundred in 5 games
The news from the Australian camp is that Mahli Beardman - the hero of the first ODI - is being rested for this encounter to tightly manage the workload.
Australia have won the toss and have opted to field
Marsh: We are going to bowl first. Mahli didn't bowl very well, so he is out today (smiles). Young kid is resting.
Brook: We would have bowled as well but we need to do both aspects of the game well. We have to be positive when they having a good phase. Sonny Baker is in for Jamie Overton.
